svg.title: MongoDB
svg.desc: MongoDB. A document database: JSON-like documents with flexible schemas, replica sets for failover and sharding to scale out. Step 1, Where it sits: Catalog writes products of any shape through the driver; change streams feed search and analytics. Step 2, Documents and indexes: find walks the compound index and reads 2 of 4 documents; the pipeline counts gifts per brand. Step 3, Replica set and failover: w: majority acks at 2 of 3 members. m1 fails, m2 wins the election, the driver retries the update. Step 4, Sharding and the limits: Sharded on hashed sku: a query with sku hits 1 of 2 shards, any other hits both. Then the limits.

g.text: Catalog writes products of any shape through the driver; change streams feed search and analytics.
find walks the compound index and reads 2 of 4 documents; the pipeline counts gifts per brand.
w: majority acks at 2 of 3 members. m1 fails, m2 wins the election, the driver retries the update.
Sharded on hashed sku: a query with sku hits 1 of 2 shards, any other hits both. Then the limits.
database catalog · collection products · every product carries its own attributes
collection products · 4 documents · indexes: _id and one compound index
replica set rs0 · the driver sends every write to the primary · w: "majority" = 2 of 3 members
after 10 s with no primary; median ≤ 12 s
updateOne({ sku: "LAMP-4" }, { $set: { price: 39 } }) · retried on m2
sh.shardCollection("catalog.products", { sku: "hashed" }) · the balancer spreads the chunks over the shards
find({ sku: "MUG-1" }) · equality on the shard key
The Catalog service writes each product as one document through the driver: a mug, a T-shirt and an e-book carry different attributes,
and the collection takes all of them. The write is acknowledged once a majority holds it, then change streams pass it on.
The compound index keeps colour, then price, in order: the query reads one short range of it and fetches 2 documents instead of scanning all 4.
The pipeline runs on the server. A write to one document is atomic, nested fields included; multi-document transactions exist but cost more.
The primary records each write in its oplog; the secondaries copy the oplog and apply it. w: "majority" acknowledges once 2 of the 3 have it.
m1 fails: after electionTimeoutMillis (10 s by default) the secondaries elect m2, and the driver retries the update once on the new primary.
Each shard is a replica set. mongos sends a query with an equality match on sku to the one shard that owns it, any other to every shard, and merges.
